## formal
Call a signature $(p,q)$ causal if $\min(p,q) = 1$, and let $\beta$ add eight directions of the majority sign: $\beta(p,q) = (p+8,q)$ if $p > q$, $(p,q+8)$ if $q > p$. Let $M_{L}$ represent residues $6, 2, 1, 7, 3, 5$ by $(1,3), (3,1), (2,1), (1,2), (4,1), (1,4)$, the lowest causal member of each (the representatives Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p3-nearest-dimension-representatives} gives these residues), and let $M_{8}$ agree with $M_{L}$ except at residues $3$ and $5$, where it takes $(12,1)$ and $(1,12)$; residues $0$ and $4$ are treated alike in both, by the costed single-ideal clause of Observation \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule}(vi).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The shift splits off a real matrix factor; proved, exact.)} For a causal $s = (p,q)$ of dimension $n$ let $\omega_{8}$ be the product of the eight added vectors of $\beta s$. Then $\omega_{8}^{2} = 1$, the elements $a_{i} = e_{i}\omega_{8}$ ($i \le n$) obey the relations of $\Cl(p,q)$, are fixed by reversion and commute with the eight added vectors, and $\Cl(\beta s) = A \otimes B$ with $A = \langle a_{i}\rangle \cong \Cl(p,q)$ and $B$ the algebra of the added vectors, $B \cong \Mat(16,\R)$, reversion acting factor by factor; $B$ has a primitive idempotent $f$ with $\widetilde{f} = f$ and $fBf = \R f$, so its reversion pairing on $Bf$ is symmetric. Hence $\Cl(\beta s) \cong \Mat(16, \Cl(s))$ with its reversion, and $s$, $\beta s$ have the same residue, causality, dimension mod $8$, pseudoscalar square and centrality, Clifford type, constituent field and reversion-pairing type. Not invariant: the complex Witt index $\lfloor(n+2)/2\rfloor$ of the conformal space $\hatV$, the stored number of ladder pairs, rises by $4$, and with it the content the gauge-algebra rule computes.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Residues $3$ and $5$: both are models of the descent's premises; proved.)} $M_{L}$ and $M_{8}$ each satisfy every premise of the window-sensitive results other than P3: F1 to F4, the eight-tower clock, the single-clock filter, Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point} (one frozen point and one metric; its orientation clause acts on residues $2$ and $6$, shared by the models, and no odd tower is oriented in either), Premise \claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference} (each model is closed under reversal), the costed clause, H1, H2 and Hypothesis (S) (stated for every signature), Premise \claimref{dark-tower-matter.u-transposition-rule} (U) (at $(12,1)$ and $(1,12)$ the field is $\HH$, which supplies the unit for the five pairs beyond the two real ones), the anomaly import (odd dimensions carry no local anomaly), the inverse-square law (no tower's unshared direction carries the one metric), R1 and R3 in their dimension-generic form, and R2 in its dimension-generic reading (its stated list of dimensions $2$, $3$, $4$ is P3's window, which $M_{8}$ leaves); the remaining postulates of the cone do not mention a tower's dimension beyond $n \bmod 4$, which $\beta$ preserves. So nothing in the descent, P3 aside, fixes the five-dimensional towers' dimension; $\beta$ can be iterated, giving a model with those towers at dimension $5 + 8k$ for every $k \ge 0$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Residues $1$ and $7$: Premise U fixes the window; proved, given U.)} Along residues $1$ and $7$ the constituent field is $\R$ in every causal member (\claimref{dark-tower-matter.constituents-field}, invariant under $\beta$ by (i)), the real Witt index of $\hatV$ is $2$ and the stored pair count is $\lfloor(n+2)/2\rfloor$ (\claimref{synthesis.gauge-algebra-by-tower}), which exceeds $2$ for $n > 3$. U3 requires the unit that builds each further pair to lie in the field, which $\R$ cannot supply; the conformal pseudoscalar along residue $7$ is central of square $-1$ but odd and does not act on the constituent ideal (\claimref{dark-tower-matter.residue-seven-unit}). So U admits only $(2,1)$ and $(1,2)$: at residues $1$ and $7$ the lowest-causal clause of P3 follows from Premise U, and P3 is not needed there.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The stored selector that separates the models.)} Premise (W) of \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-complement-window-lowest-causal} admits every representative of $M_{L}$ and neither shifted representative of $M_{8}$; up to dimension sixteen the lowest causal member is the only admitted causal member of each odd residue. (W) is not in the premise set; it was found with the fit known and is not adopted.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Cost.)} With R1 to R3 read in their dimension-generic form (share $V_{3}/V_{D}$ for a space of dimension $D$, one cell radius per unshared direction), the dark-to-baryon ratio is $(11\pi + 16)/3\pi \in (5.36, 5.37)$ in $M_{L}$ and $1 + 8/3 + 1920/\pi^{5} \in (9.9, 10.0)$ in $M_{8}$. The five-dimensional towers' dimension is therefore a recorded input of the unit-ball relation, selected among the models by the observed ratio, and P3 stays a costed premise for residues $3$ and $5$; the results stored under P3 about the five-dimensional towers' content hold given P3.
\end{enumerate}

## technical
Every residue mod 8 has infinitely many causal signatures, spaced by eight dimensions along each sign. Multiplying each old generator by the product of eight new ones of the majority sign gives a copy of the old algebra that commutes with the new eight, which generate a sixteen by sixteen real matrix algebra; so the shifted algebra is the old one tensored with real matrices, reversion included, and residue, causality, flag bit, real chirality, anomaly parity, pairing type and the constituents' field are unchanged. The number of ladder pairs, the complex Witt index of the conformal space, is not unchanged: it grows by four. At residues 3 and 5 that does no harm, since the constituents' field is the quaternions, which supply the unit each extra pair needs; a second model of every premise other than P3 puts the five-dimensional towers at dimension thirteen, keeping everything else, and the dark-to-baryon ratio becomes about 9.94 instead of 5.364. At residues 1 and 7 the field is real in every causal member, so Premise U, which forbids an outside imaginary unit, admits only the three-dimensional member: there the window follows from U. The one stored hypothesis that would fix the five-dimensional window, premise (W), is not periodic and is not adopted.

## lay
The series sorts possible hidden worlds into eight families, each containing worlds of many different dimensions with a single time direction, and to predict the amount of dark matter it picks the smallest world in each family by an assumption. For the two families whose smallest worlds are three-dimensional, another assumption of the theory, that no imaginary unit may be brought in from outside, already rules out every larger world: there the choice is derived. For the two families whose smallest worlds are five-dimensional it is not: adding eight dimensions changes nothing that any other assumption looks at, and gives a different amount of dark matter (about 9.9 instead of 5.4 times the ordinary matter). So for those families the choice of the smallest world is an input that the observed amount selects, not a prediction.

## one-liner
Adding eight directions of the majority sign splits off a $\Mat(16,\R)$ factor (reversion included); at residues $3$, $5$ a second model with the towers at $(12,1)$, $(1,12)$ satisfies every premise except P3, Premise U included (field $\HH$), so that window is an input (ratio about $9.94$ instead of $5.364$), while at residues $1$, $7$ the field is $\R$ in every causal member and U admits only $(2,1)$, $(1,2)$.

proofs.proof-main.tex:
\emph{Setting.} A tower representative is a signature $(p,q)$; its residue is $p - q \bmod 8$, which the $(1,1)$ ascent preserves (Fact \claimref{dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock}). The check builds each algebra with \texttt{GA.py}, the representative's own generators first and the eight added ones last.

(i) Let $s = (p,q)$ be causal of dimension $n$, with majority sign $\sigma$ ($\sigma = +1$ if $p > q$), and let $g_{1}, \dots, g_{8}$ be the added vectors of $\beta s$, all of square $\sigma$. Their product $\omega_{8}$ has $\omega_{8}^{2} = (-1)^{28}\sigma^{8} = 1$. Each old generator $e_{i}$ anticommutes with every $g_{j}$, hence commutes with $\omega_{8}$ (eight sign changes), while each $g_{j}$ anticommutes with $\omega_{8}$ (it meets seven others). So $a_{i} = e_{i}\omega_{8}$ has $a_{i}^{2} = e_{i}^{2}\omega_{8}^{2} = e_{i}^{2}$, $a_{i}a_{k} = e_{i}e_{k}$ for $i \ne k$ (so the $a_{i}$ anticommute), and $a_{i}g_{j} = e_{i}\omega_{8}g_{j} = -e_{i}g_{j}\omega_{8} = g_{j}e_{i}\omega_{8} = g_{j}a_{i}$. Reversion fixes $a_{i}$, a blade of grade $9$ ($(-1)^{36} = 1$), and each $g_{j}$. By the universal property the relations give an algebra map $\Cl(p,q) \to A = \langle a_{i}\rangle$; the products $a_{S}$ over subsets $S$ are $\pm e_{S}$ or $\pm e_{S}\omega_{8}$, distinct blades, so it is injective. The products $a_{S}g_{T}$ over all subsets are $2^{n+8}$ distinct blades up to sign (computed for $(2,1)$ and $(4,1)$; the mirror cases differ only in the signs of the squares), so $A \otimes B \to \Cl(\beta s)$ is onto, and by dimension an isomorphism; reversion of $\Cl(\beta s)$ restricts to the reversion of $A$ (it fixes the generators $a_{i}$ and reverses products) and of $B$. $B$ is $\Cl(8,0)$ or $\Cl(0,8)$, of residue $0$, a matrix algebra over $\R$ by the imported classification (Fact \claimref{dark-tower-matter.imported-clifford-structure}), of dimension $256$, so $B \cong \Mat(16,\R)$. \emph{Computed:} with $h = g_{1234}, g_{5678}, g_{1256}, g_{1357}$ (pairwise overlaps even, so they commute; each squares to $1$ for either sign), $f = \prod\tfrac12(1 + h)$ has $f^{2} = f$, $\widetilde{f} = f$, scalar part $\tfrac1{16}$, and $fxf \in \R f$ for all $256$ blades $x$, nonzero for exactly sixteen; so $fBf = \R f$ and $f$ is primitive. For $\psi, \varphi \in Bf$, $\widetilde{\psi}\varphi = c(\psi,\varphi)f$, and reversing gives $c(\varphi,\psi)f = c(\psi,\varphi)\widetilde{f} = c(\psi,\varphi)f$: the reversion pairing on $Bf \cong \R^{16}$ is symmetric. Therefore $\Cl(\beta s) \cong A \otimes \Mat(16,\R) \cong \Mat(16, \Cl(s))$, Morita equivalent to $\Cl(s)$ (Fact \claimref{tower.morita-equivalence-algebra-amplification}); its minimal left ideals are $S \otimes Bf$ with $S$ one of $A$, and its reversion pairing is that of $S$ tensored with a symmetric form, of the same symmetry type. The type data: $\beta$ adds $8$ to $p - q$ or subtracts it, so the residue is unchanged; $\min$ stays $1$; $n$ changes by $8$; the pseudoscalar square $(-1)^{n(n-1)/2}(-1)^{q}$ is multiplied by $(-1)^{8n + 28}$, and by $(-1)^{8}$ when $q$ grows, both equal to $1$ (computed for the four odd representatives); for odd $n$ the pseudoscalar is central in both (computed). Reversal $(p,q) \mapsto (q,p)$ commutes with $\beta$, since it exchanges the majority sign. The constituent field, the division ring of $\Cl^{0}(\hatV) \cong \Cl(p+1,q)$ (\claimref{dark-tower-matter.constituents-field}), is unchanged, since (i) applied to $(p+1,q)$ splits off the same $\Mat(16,\R)$. \emph{Not invariant:} $\hatV$ has dimension $n + 2$, so its complex Witt index $\lfloor(n+2)/2\rfloor$, the stored number of ladder pairs (\claimref{synthesis.gauge-algebra-by-tower}), rises by $4$ ($2 \to 6$ at residues $1$, $7$, $3 \to 7$ at residues $3$, $5$; computed), while its real Witt index stays $2$; a Witt index of $\hatV$ over $\C$ is not a Morita invariant of $\Cl(s)$, and the gauge-algebra rule, which reads it, gives different content at $s$ and $\beta s$.

(ii) Premise by premise, at the pinned versions, for $M_{L}$ and $M_{8}$, which differ only at residues $3$ and $5$. \emph{F1 to F4.} The foundation's directions with sign bits generate $\Cl(p,q)$ for every signature; the check confirms the Clifford relations of every representative of both models. \emph{The clock.} Every representative of both models has the residue it represents (computed). \emph{The single-clock filter.} All populated representatives are causal in both (computed). \emph{P1} (\claimref{dark-matter.p1-single-frozen-point}). It freezes one $I$ and couples every tower to one metric; it places no condition on a tower's signature (as \claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-complement-window-lowest-causal} records, nothing in the series says the towers' spacetimes lie in the frozen point's complement). Its orientation clause acts on the reversal orbit $\{2, 6\}$, whose representatives $(3,1)$, $(1,3)$ are the same in both models and have dimension $0 \bmod 4$, so both carry the flag (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.oriented-causal-towers-mirror-pair-every-window}: oriented exactly when $n \equiv 0 \pmod 4$); the odd representatives have odd dimension in both, so no odd tower is oriented in either. \emph{P2} (\claimref{dark-matter.p2-indifference}). It equates towers only along $r \mapsto -r$ and reaches labels; each model assigns to $-r$ the reversal of its signature for $r$ (computed), and the labels (residues and tower charges) are the same in both. \emph{The costed clause.} Residues $0$ and $4$ are treated alike in both models. \emph{H1, H2, (S).} H1 defines momentum on a spinor ideal of any signature; H2 identifies a tower's gauge algebra with the automorphisms of its hierarchy, and (S) makes the slots fermionic; all three are stated for every tower, so they hold at $(12,1)$ and $(1,12)$, where the content they produce differs (seven pairs, by (i)); the stored computations of that content (\claimref{synthesis.gauge-algebra-by-tower}) are made in dimensions three to five and do not apply at thirteen. \emph{Premise U} (\claimref{dark-tower-matter.u-transposition-rule}). (U1) and (U2) are definitions valid in every tower. (U3) asks that every complex unit building a ladder pair lie in the constituent field. At $(12,1)$ and $(1,12)$ the field is $\HH$, as at $(4,1)$, $(1,4)$ (by (i)); the real Witt index $2$ gives two real pairs and the other five need a unit, which $\HH$ supplies (a unit $u \in \HH$, with pair scalars $\mathrm{span}\{1, u\}$ as in the stored rule at dimension five), so U3 holds. \emph{Anomaly import.} Local gauge and gravitational anomaly forms have degree $n + 2$ and exist only in even dimension (and the gravitational one only for $n \equiv 2 \pmod 4$, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.residues-zero-four-real-chirality-anomaly}(i), (ii)); the odd representatives have odd $n$ in both models. The anomaly obstruction of that theorem's clause (iii) concerns residue $0$ at $(1,1)$, which the costed clause treats alike in both. \emph{Inverse-square law.} It bounds an extra direction carrying the one metric; in both models the towers' unshared directions are their own (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.thickness-not-gravitational-quantity}), so it is met alike. \emph{R1 to R3.} R1 and R3 are dimension-generic and hold in both. R2 as stated lists the dimensions $2$, $3$, $4$, the window P3 supplies; $M_{8}$ meets R2 only in its dimension-generic reading (one quantum per unit ball of a tower's own space, of any dimension), which is the reading used here and in (v). \emph{The remaining postulates of the cone.} T14's (U) on the rank-one eigenvalues at the ceiling, P4 (the same asymmetry on every oriented tower), P5 (what boundary modes return), CPT covariance, the flag as datum, the interface premise (I), (P), (Q), (R), the rate inputs (L, U), the slot-module hypothesis (this tower's composites), the common-ceiling premise (the reversal pair), tameness, the indifference premise and the frozen-point, tractor and field-theory imports: none mentions a tower's dimension beyond $n \bmod 4$, which $\beta$ preserves, or concerns the five-dimensional towers' signature, so each is met or not alike in both models. \emph{Selectors.} The flag bit reads $n \bmod 4$, real chirality reads $n \bmod 4$ and the pseudoscalar, the anomaly degree reads $n$'s parity and $n \bmod 4$, the pairing type reads the reversion form, the field reads $\Cl^{0}(\hatV)$: all unchanged by (i); the pair count changes but no premise bounds it at residues $3$, $5$. So no premise other than P3 separates the models; iterating $\beta$ at residues $3$ and $5$ gives a model for every $k \ge 0$ with the five-dimensional towers at dimension $5 + 8k$ (the check confirms U3 at all five causal members of each up to dimension $21$, of dimensions $5$, $7$, $13$, $15$, $21$).

(iii) Along residues $1$ and $7$ the causal members are $(2 + 8k, 1)$, $(1, 8 + 8k)$ at residue $1$ and their reversals at residue $7$. The check computes, for every causal member of an odd residue up to dimension $21$, the real Witt index of $\hatV = (p+1, q+1)$ from the Gram matrix of its generators (it is $2$, $\min(p+1, q+1)$ with $\min(p,q) = 1$) and the field by the stored rule (division ring of $\Cl(p+1, q)$ by its residue, which reproduces the table of \claimref{dark-tower-matter.constituents-field} at the lowest members: $\C$, $\C$, $\R$, $\R$, $\HH$, $\HH$ at residues $6, 2, 1, 7, 3, 5$). At residues $1$ and $7$ the field is $\R$ in every member, and the pair count $\lfloor(n+2)/2\rfloor$ equals the real Witt index $2$ only at $n = 3$; for $n > 3$ at least one pair needs a complex unit, $\R$ supplies none, and U3 forbids adjoining one. The conformal pseudoscalar along residue $7$ is central of square $-1$ (computed at $(1,10)$, $\Cl(2,11)$), but it has odd grade $n + 2$ and carries the even ideal to the odd one (\claimref{dark-tower-matter.residue-seven-unit}(ii)), so it does not act on the constituent ideal and is not an element of the field. Hence U3 admits exactly $(2,1)$ at residue $1$ and $(1,2)$ at residue $7$ among causal members (computed up to dimension $21$; for every $n > 3$ by the argument), and at residues $3$ and $5$ it admits every causal member. The lowest-causal clause at residues $1$ and $7$ thus follows from Premise U with the stored pair count; it is not independent of the premises.

(iv) Under (W) with $\Lambda > 0$ a causal signature is admitted exactly when $\max(p,q) \le 4$ (\claimref{synthesis.frozen-point-complement-window-lowest-causal}(ii), (iii)). Every representative of $M_{L}$ passes; $(12,1)$ and $(1,12)$ fail. An enumeration of all causal signatures of odd residue up to dimension sixteen finds exactly one admitted member per residue, the lowest. (W) is a selector that is not periodic along a residue, which (ii) shows the descent lacks at residues $3$ and $5$.

(v) With $V_{2k} = \pi^{k}/k!$ and $V_{2k+1} = 2^{k+1}\pi^{k}/(2k+1)!!$, the shares $V_{3}/V_{D}$ are $4/3$ ($D = 2$), $8/3\pi$ ($D = 4$) and $960/\pi^{5}$ ($D = 12$), with the mirror's share $1$ in both models. So the ratio is $1 + 8/3 + 16/3\pi = (11\pi + 16)/3\pi$ in $M_{L}$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-matter.unit-ball-rule}) and $1 + 8/3 + 1920/\pi^{5}$ in $M_{8}$. The check brackets both with $\tfrac{333}{106} < \pi < \tfrac{355}{113}$: $(5.36, 5.37)$ and $(9.9, 10.0)$, disjoint. Since the observed ratio is the only datum separating the models, the five-dimensional towers' dimension is an input that the fit selects, which is the status Observation \claimref{dark-matter.status-rule} records for the relation; P3 remains a premise for residues $3$ and $5$, with its lowest-causal clause there shown independent of the descent, while at residues $1$ and $7$ it is a consequence of Premise U by (iii).

check_py:
"""Exact checks: the descent leaves the five-dimensional towers' dimension free; Premise U fixes the
three-dimensional ones.

Two models of the window-sensitive premises, identical except at residues 3 and 5:
M_L puts residues 1, 7, 3, 5 at their lowest causal members (2,1), (1,2), (4,1), (1,4) (P3's choice);
M_8 agrees with M_L except at residues 3 and 5, where it takes the Bott shifts (12,1), (1,12). Both put
residue 6 at this world (1,3), residue 2 at its reversal (3,1), and leave residues 0 and 4 to the costed
single-ideal clause. The shift itself is checked at all four odd residues (an algebra fact); at residues 1 and 7
Premise U (U3) with the stored pair count admits only the lowest causal member, checked over all causal
members up to dimension 21 (real Witt index of the conformal space from GA Gram matrices, field by residue).
The shift beta adds eight directions of the majority sign. The checks build each algebra in GA.py with
squares tuples (the representative's own generators first, then the eight added ones) and verify:
the split Cl(beta s) = A (x) B with A = <e_i w8> a copy of Cl(s), B = Cl(8,0) or Cl(0,8), [A, B] = 0,
reversion restricting to each factor; that B is the real matrix algebra of size 16 (a primitive
idempotent f with f~ = f and f B f = R f on all 256 blades); the type data every stored selector reads
(residue, causality, reversal, n mod 4, pseudoscalar square and centrality); the premises' conditions on
both models; the unit-ball ratio of each model by rational bounds on pi; and that (W) holds in M_L only.
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F
from itertools import combinations

import GA
from tp_premise import premise

PI_LO, PI_HI = F(333, 106), F(355, 113)

M_L = {6: (1, 3), 2: (3, 1), 1: (2, 1), 7: (1, 2), 3: (4, 1), 5: (1, 4)}
ODD = (1, 7, 3, 5)


def beta(s):
    p, q = s
    return (p + 8, q) if p > q else (p, q + 8)


SHIFTED = (3, 5)
M_8 = {r: (beta(s) if r in SHIFTED else s) for r, s in M_L.items()}


def squares(s, shifted):
    p, q = s
    base = tuple([1] * p + [-1] * q)
    if not shifted:
        return base
    return base + tuple([1 if p > q else -1] * 8)


def residue(s):
    return (s[0] - s[1]) % 8


def causal(s):
    return min(s) == 1


def blade(*ix):
    return {tuple(sorted(ix)): F(1)}


def top_square(sq):
    c, b = GA.blade_mul(tuple(range(len(sq))), tuple(range(len(sq))), sq)
    assert b == ()
    return c


def check_bott_shift_splits_off_a_real_matrix_factor():
    """beta s has Cl(beta s) = A (x) B: A generated by e_i w8 (i < n) obeys Cl(s), B = the eight added
    generators, every a_i commutes with every b_j, w8^2 = 1, and reversion fixes each a_i."""
    premise("tower.morita-equivalence-algebra-amplification")
    premise("dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock")
    for r in ODD:
        s = M_L[r]
        n = s[0] + s[1]
        sq = squares(s, True)
        assert len(sq) == n + 8
        w8 = blade(*range(n, n + 8))
        assert GA.eq(GA.mul(w8, w8, sq), GA.sc(1))
        a = [GA.mul(GA.gen(i), w8, sq) for i in range(n)]
        for i in range(n):
            assert GA.eq(GA.mul(a[i], a[i], sq), GA.sc(squares(s, False)[i]))
            assert GA.eq(GA.reverse(a[i]), a[i])
            for j in range(i + 1, n):
                assert GA.anticommutes(a[i], a[j], sq)
            for k in range(n, n + 8):
                assert GA.commutes(a[i], GA.gen(k), sq)
        # the volume of A is the pseudoscalar of s times a power of w8: same square as Cl(s)'s
        vol = GA.sc(1)
        for x in a:
            vol = GA.mul(vol, x, sq)
        assert GA.eq(GA.mul(vol, vol, sq), GA.sc(top_square(squares(s, False))))
        GA.check(f"Cl{beta(s)} = Cl{s} (x) Cl(8 of one sign), factors commute", True)


def check_tensor_split_is_an_isomorphism():
    """The 2^n products of the a_i and the 2^8 products of the added generators multiply to 2^(n+8)
    distinct basis blades up to sign: A (x) B -> Cl(beta s) is onto, so (by dimension) an isomorphism,
    and A is a faithful copy of Cl(s)."""
    premise("tower.morita-equivalence-algebra-amplification")
    for r in (1, 3):
        s = M_L[r]
        n = s[0] + s[1]
        sq = squares(s, True)
        w8 = tuple(range(n, n + 8))
        seen = set()
        for k in range(n + 1):
            for S in combinations(range(n), k):
                aS = GA.sc(1)
                for i in S:
                    aS = GA.mul(aS, GA.mul(GA.gen(i), {w8: F(1)}, sq), sq)
                assert len(aS) == 1
                for T in GA.all_blades(8):
                    prod = GA.mul(aS, {tuple(n + j for j in T): F(1)}, sq)
                    assert len(prod) == 1
                    (b, c), = prod.items()
                    assert c in (1, -1)
                    seen.add(b)
        assert len(seen) == 2 ** (n + 8)
        GA.check(f"A (x) B spans Cl{beta(s)}: {len(seen)} blades", True)


def _primitive_idempotent(sq):
    hs = [blade(0, 1, 2, 3), blade(4, 5, 6, 7), blade(0, 1, 4, 5), blade(0, 2, 4, 6)]
    f = GA.sc(1)
    for h in hs:
        assert GA.eq(GA.mul(h, h, sq), GA.sc(1))
        f = GA.mul(f, GA.scal(F(1, 2), GA.add(GA.sc(1), h)), sq)
    for h in hs:
        for g in hs:
            assert GA.commutes(h, g, sq)
    return f


def check_eight_of_one_sign_is_real_sixteen_by_sixteen():
    """Cl(8,0) and Cl(0,8): f = prod (1 + h_k)/2 over four commuting blades of square 1 is a nonzero
    idempotent with f~ = f, f has 16 terms of scalar part 1/16, and f x f is a real multiple of f for all
    256 blades x, so f B f = R f: B is Mat(16, R) with the reversion pairing on B f symmetric."""
    premise("dark-tower-matter.imported-clifford-structure")
    for sign in (1, -1):
        sq = tuple([sign] * 8)
        f = _primitive_idempotent(sq)
        assert GA.eq(GA.mul(f, f, sq), f)
        assert GA.eq(GA.reverse(f), f)
        assert len(f) == 16 and f[()] == F(1, 16)
        mult = 0
        for b in GA.all_blades(8):
            y = GA.mul(GA.mul(f, {b: F(1)}, sq), f, sq)
            c = y.get((), F(0)) * 16
            assert GA.eq(y, GA.scal(c, f))
            if c != 0:
                mult += 1
        assert mult == 16
        GA.check(f"Cl(8 of sign {sign}) has f B f = R f, 16 blades survive", True)


def check_type_data_invariant_and_pair_count_not():
    """For each odd representative s and beta s: same residue, both causal, beta commutes with reversal,
    n mod 4 equal (so the flag bit and real chirality agree), pseudoscalar square equal, pseudoscalar
    central in both (odd n), the single time on the same sign."""
    premise("dark-matter.imported-eight-towers-mod-8-clock")
    premise("synthesis.oriented-causal-towers-mirror-pair-every-window")
    premise("synthesis.residues-zero-four-real-chirality-anomaly")
    for r in ODD:
        s, t = M_L[r], beta(M_L[r])
        assert residue(s) == residue(t) == r
        assert causal(s) and causal(t)
        assert beta((s[1], s[0])) == (t[1], t[0])
        n, m = s[0] + s[1], t[0] + t[1]

        assert top_square(squares(s, False)) == top_square(squares(t, False))
        sq = squares(t, False)
        top = {tuple(range(m)): F(1)}
        for i in range(m):

        assert (s[0] < s[1]) == (t[0] < t[1])
    # not invariant: the complex Witt index of the conformal space, floor((n+2)/2), the stored pair count
    assert [(sum(M_L[r]) + 2) // 2 for r in ODD] == [2, 2, 3, 3]
    assert [(sum(beta(M_L[r])) + 2) // 2 for r in ODD] == [6, 6, 7, 7]

    for r in (2, 6):

    GA.check("type data invariant under beta on the odd residues", True)

def _ball_share_bounds(D):
    """V_3 / V_D as an interval, V_D = pi^(D/2)/(D/2)! for even D, 2^(k+1) pi^k/(2k+1)!! for D = 2k+1."""
    lo_hi = []
    for pi in (PI_LO, PI_HI):
        if D % 2 == 0:
            k, fac = D // 2, 1
            for j in range(2, k + 1):
                fac *= j
            vd = pi ** k / fac
        else:
            k, dfac = (D - 1) // 2, 1
            for j in range(3, D + 1, 2):
                dfac *= j
            vd = F(2) ** (k + 1) * pi ** k / dfac
        lo_hi.append((F(4) * pi / 3) / vd)
    return min(lo_hi), max(lo_hi)


def check_unit_ball_ratio_differs_between_models():
    """R1 to R3 in their dimension-generic form hold in both models; the ratio 1 + sum_dark V_3/V_D is
    (11 pi + 16)/(3 pi) in M_L (in (5.36, 5.37)) and 1 + 8/3 + 1920/pi^5 in M_8 (in (9.9, 10.0))."""
    out = []
    for M in (M_L, M_8):
        lo, hi = F(0), F(0)
        for r, s in M.items():
            if r == 6:
                continue
            D = s[0] + s[1] - 1
            a, b = _ball_share_bounds(D)
            lo, hi = lo + a, hi + b
        out.append((lo, hi))
    (l1, h1), (l2, h2) = out
    assert F(536, 100) < l1 and h1 < F(537, 100)
    assert F(99, 10) < l2 and h2 < F(10)
    assert (l2 - 1 - F(8, 3), h2 - 1 - F(8, 3)) == (1920 / PI_HI ** 5, 1920 / PI_LO ** 5)
    assert h1 < l2
    # closed forms: V_3/V_2 = 4/3, V_3/V_4 = 8/(3 pi), V_3/V_10 = 160/pi^4, V_3/V_12 = 960/pi^5
    assert _ball_share_bounds(2) == (F(4, 3), F(4, 3))
    assert _ball_share_bounds(4) == (F(8, 3) / PI_HI, F(8, 3) / PI_LO)
    assert _ball_share_bounds(10) == (160 / PI_HI ** 4, 160 / PI_LO ** 4)
    assert _ball_share_bounds(12) == (960 / PI_HI ** 5, 960 / PI_LO ** 5)
    GA.check("unit-ball ratio: M_L about 5.364, M_8 about 9.94", True)


def check_w_admits_m_l_and_not_m_8():

def field_of(s):
    """Constituent field: the division ring of Cl^0(hatV) = Cl(p+1, q), by its residue (stored rule)."""
    r = (s[0] + 1 - s[1]) % 8
    return "R" if r in (0, 1, 2) else ("C" if r in (3, 7) else "H")


def real_witt_index_of_conformal_space(s):
    p, q = s
    sq = GA.sig(p + 1, q + 1)
    gram = [[GA.dot(GA.gen(i), GA.gen(j), sq) for j in range(len(sq))] for i in range(len(sq))]
    pos, neg, zero = GA.congruence_signature(gram)
    assert zero == 0
    return min(pos, neg)


def check_premise_u_admits_the_shift_only_at_residues_three_and_five():
    """U3: every complex unit that builds a ladder pair lies in the constituent's field. With b = floor((n+2)/2)
    pairs (complex Witt index of hatV) and real Witt index 2, b - 2 pairs need a unit. The field rule
    reproduces the stored table at the lowest members (R at 1, 7; H at 3, 5) and is unchanged by beta. Over
    all causal members up to dimension 21, U3 holds at residues 1 and 7 only at (2,1) and (1,2), and at every
    member of residues 3 and 5. At (1,10) the conformal pseudoscalar is central of square -1 but odd."""
    premise("synthesis.gauge-algebra-by-tower")
    premise("dark-tower-matter.constituents-field")
    premise("dark-tower-matter.residue-seven-unit")
    assert [field_of(M_L[r]) for r in (6, 2, 1, 7, 3, 5)] == ["C", "C", "R", "R", "H", "H"]
    admitted = {r: [] for r in ODD}
    for n in range(3, 22):
        for p in range(1, n):
            s = (p, n - p)
            r = residue(s)
            if r not in ODD or not causal(s):
                continue
            assert real_witt_index_of_conformal_space(s) == 2
            assert field_of(s) == field_of(M_L[r])
            b = (n + 2) // 2
            if b == 2 or field_of(s) in ("C", "H"):
                admitted[r].append(s)
    assert admitted[1] == [(2, 1)] and admitted[7] == [(1, 2)]
    assert admitted[3][0] == (4, 1) and admitted[5][0] == (1, 4)
    assert (12, 1) in admitted[3] and (1, 12) in admitted[5]
    assert len(admitted[3]) == 5 and len(admitted[5]) == 5
    # the residue-seven pseudoscalar at (1,10): conformal Cl(2,11), central, square -1, odd grade
    sq = GA.sig(2, 11)
    top = {tuple(range(13)): F(1)}
    assert GA.eq(GA.mul(top, top, sq), GA.sc(-1))
    assert all(GA.commutes(top, GA.gen(i), sq) for i in range(13))
    assert len(next(iter(top))) % 2 == 1
    GA.check("U3 admits only the lowest member at residues 1, 7 and every member at 3, 5", True)
